negatives.text: New formula, terrible product.. Pretty angry with the quality of this product. I usually buy these once a year and my fruit fly problem is solved overnight. This year the infestation got out of control, but not to worry, I’d just reorder the best lures out there! Imagine my surprise when the packaging is a little different this time around and the lure smells like straight up apple cider vinegar. My wife had tried homemade ACV traps before we bought these, but I assured her these Terro traps would work better. Instead I’m pretty sure this is just all vinegar now. They are refillable despite the vendors disengenuious response that they are not.. The product itself is fine. It's not rocket science as many variants are on the market. Why do I rate it a 2 you might ask. When I submitted a question as to whether these are refillable or not the official representative response from the seller was simple: NO . That was it a NO. I then read some reviews and many of them included the fact they are refillable so I ordered them as the price and quantity were acceptable for my needs. Great lure; horrible trap. These are great at luring the fruit flies. But horrible at trapping them. Minutes after putting it out there were dozens buzzing around it and crawling on it, into it.... and then right back out of it. The holes and slots are just WAY to big. 24 hours later, I had only 2 dead ones in it and dozens still around the kitchen. The bait just smells like apple cider vinegar. So in the end I'm just going to make the classic trap of apple cider vinegar in a mason jar, a drop of dish soap, and a Saran wrap cover with some holes poked in it. Minimally useful: bait traps are tiny! You must kill them all—or you are wasting your time & money. The traps look like tiny miniature red plastic apples, with slits on top. They sit quietly wherever placed; they have trapped fruit flies; however it’s annoying to see MORE fruit flies perched on top of the traps! You fill each of them with a liquid chemical which comes packaged separately. I guess you also have to wipe each one, so there’s no attractant on the outside. This was a waste of money—I have MORE fruit flies, than before! IMO, they’re ridiculously small! Obviously, there’s more to thi

SCAM- IT IS JUST VINEGAR. Scam. It is a plastic apple and the "bait" is vinegar. It does work, but so does the dish of vinegar I put out to test it and that is $2 for 16 oz. If you feel the need to have a "cute" plastic thing to put vinegar in for $13, go for it. I will be getting my money back. This is why Americans are in debt, overpriced trash like this.

I like old design better. I don’t like the new design. Picture is of the new design. I just feel like the bugs can get out a lot easier which then means that I’m relying on the liquid in the trap a lot more. I still have one with the old design, with round holes on the top no lines, and it catches a lot of the fruit flies.

Didn’t last very long. Effective as long as there is fluid in them. I set out the four traps on July 25th, in various locations around my house, and they were all bone dry less than a month later. FWIW, my house stays around 45% relative humidity. I suspect that the 180-day claim is only valid if you use these one at a time, and in controlled, humid, laboratory conditions. I did have one very slowly leak vinegar through the clear disk in the bottom of the trap. It left a ring on the sink where it was sitting. It would be prudent to take care in where you place these, just in case …

Just ok. One lure pack did not last 30 days, so a 4 pack last not even 120 days. It sat on the windowsill above my sink. It was not in direct or indirect sunlight. I only got about 6 fruit flies. It’s 10/4 , purchased 8/30 used 2 lures and I’m still trying to kill several that fly around but don’t go in. Trying to decide which other product to try.

Not working. I have purchased these before & they seemed to work but this shipment doesn’t work at all! The liquid used to come in lille bottles but this time in plastic “blister caps”! Not sure if from a different vendor or just changing their formula! Wont buy again!

Not working as well as Terro from Lowes. I bought a 2-pack of these at Lowes last year, and they worked great. Not sure what the deal is with this 6-pack I purchased this year, but I've used three and they have very few fruit flys in them at all. My wife opened a spoiled bottle of wine the other day, and before we dumped it I put a little in the Terro 'apple'. That drew more flys than the previous three apples.
